Anthracnose.quote: Infected fruits have black, circular, sunken cankers of different sizes.
The first symptoms of anthracnose are spots on the leaves that begin as yellowish or water-soaked areas that enlarge and turn brown to black.
Lesions that are elongated and sunken can also develop on petioles and stems of plants which can result in the death of developing fruit.

Choanephora_Fruit_Rot.quote: Symptoms are usually found on the blossom end of the fruit, with the initial symptom being a soft, wet rot.
A gray-to-black whisker appearance will cover the rotted area of the fruit.

Downy_Mildew.quote: Symptoms first appear on the upper leaf surface as angular, vein-bounded, yellow to pale-green spots, turning brown and coalescing to turn entire leaves brown with disease progression.
Signs and symptoms of downy mildew typically occur only on leaves.

Phytophthora_Blight.quote: Symptoms on cucumber, muskmelon, and watermelon are normally found on leaves and fruit, while the disease affects all parts of pumpkin and squash.
Elongated, soft lesions occur on the stem close to the soil line and may extend several inches upward... these lesions girdle stems, resulting in rapid wilting and death of affected plants.
Circular lesions are common on fruit and will appear water-soaked and sunken, and can be wet or slimy with a thin layer of mycelium and sporangia.

Plectosphaerella_Fungus.quote: The symptoms associated with this disease problem include root rot, crown rot, and vascular discoloration in the stems, leading to a severe late season wilt and plant collapse.
